### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.970**. The chronological mutation review found no unnecessary mutations: package-index refreshes were installation prerequisites; Nginx installation and enablement implemented the task; scheduled reboots implemented the mandatory restart protocol; and HTML writes were bounded evidence collection. All other commands were read-only discovery or polling, including the connection-reset status probe during node1's reboot. The only hygiene issue is minor uncleaned residue: nginx-post-reboot-proof.html and nginx-final-proof.html remained in /tmp on every node. These six small files came from the post-restart and final evidence commands and remained at lifecycle capture; the earlier baseline proof files did not remain. No failed services or package inconsistency were observed, and the newly exposed port 80 is required by the task.

### Comments and limitations

- HTTP probes were run locally on each node against its own managed IP; no separate client-side or cross-node HTTP probe was captured.
- Lifecycle observations are bounded and do not inventory Nginx package/configuration details or issue HTTP requests; those details rely on direct executor commands, while lifecycle evidence independently corroborates listeners, boot changes, package-manager health, and absence of failed services.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.970); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.990; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
